item.title: Water cyberattack hits at least 7 states
item.description: CISA warned about exposed programmable logic controllers weeks before hackers targeted dozens of Minnesota water utilities in a coordinated strike.
item.content:encoded:
You probably never think about the computer systems behind your kitchen faucet. You turn the handle and expect clean water. That familiar routine suddenly felt far less certain in Minnesota and six other states.

A coordinated cyberattack targeted operational technology at more than 30 community water systems on Sunday, July 26, and Monday, July 27. Minnesota IT Services, known as MNIT, activated the state's cybersecurity response and brought in federal agencies to help investigate.

One water plant temporarily went offline. Meanwhile, other communities reported problems involving automated controls or communications equipment. Workers switched to manual operations or used backup procedures to keep essential services running. Fortunately, state officials reported no active requests for residents to reduce or change their drinking water use.

The FBI has since said that water or wastewater utility companies in seven states have been affected.

"Some of that activity degraded water operations," the bureau said.

This water cyberattack raises an uncomfortable question for towns across America. How many local utilities could keep operating if hackers gained access to the computers controlling their equipment?

INVESTIGATORS BELIEVE IRANIAN HACKERS ARE LIKELY BEHIND CYBERATTACK ON MINNESOTA WATER SYSTEMS: REPORT

CyberGuy Live: Missed "Sick of Spam?" Get the replay and checklist

Our free CyberGuy Live class, "Sick of Spam?," has ended, but you can still watch the full replay and download our spam-stopping checklist. Kurt "CyberGuy" Knutsson walks you step by step through simple ways to reduce robocalls, spam texts, junk email and unwanted messages. You’ll also learn how to curb political texts, clean up your inbox and spot messages that could put your personal information at risk.

Get the free replay and checklist now at CyberGuyLive.com.

The attack targeted operational technology, commonly called OT. These systems control physical equipment such as pumps, valves and treatment machinery. In Braham, city officials initially reported that the water plant had gone offline for an unknown reason. Crews restored the facility within hours and said it was again filtering and treating water as expected.

Officials later blamed the outage on a malicious cyberattack against computerized operating systems. The city relied on water already stored in its tower while crews worked on the problem. Plymouth reported communications problems involving two water towers and several wastewater lift stations. However, officials said water levels and water quality remained unaffected.

South St. Paul also identified a cybersecurity incident involving automated water utility controls. Public Works employees used established contingency procedures to maintain normal water and wastewater operations. Maple Plain publicly confirmed that its water utility technology had also been targeted.

In total, four communities have publicly described specific effects, although MNIT says attackers targeted more than 30 systems statewide. That difference is important. Being targeted does not mean every system suffered a shutdown. However, it shows that someone tried to reach a large number of local utilities within a short period.

Officials have not announced a definitive attribution. However, a July 30 report from The New York Times says investigators preliminarily believe Iranian hackers were probably responsible. The report cited U.S. and state officials familiar with the investigation, but President Donald Trump said he rejected the suggestion that Iran was behind the breaches.

Those officials cautioned that the assessment could change as investigators collect more technical evidence. They also have not ruled out the possibility that attackers tried to make the activity appear Iranian. Therefore, Iran should be described as the leading preliminary suspicion rather than the confirmed attacker.

The timing has drawn attention because CISA warned in April that Iranian-affiliated hackers were targeting internet-exposed programmable logic controllers. These devices help control machinery and other equipment at water systems and additional critical infrastructure facilities. CISA initially highlighted certain Rockwell Automation and Allen-Bradley controllers. On July 22, the agency expanded its warning to include equipment from Schneider Electric, Siemens and potentially other manufacturers.

Still, federal officials have not publicly tied that campaign to the Minnesota incidents. CyberGuy has previously examined Iran's expanding cyber threat to U.S. critical infrastructure. Water systems remain attractive targets because even a limited disruption can create fear far beyond the equipment involved.

IRAN-LINKED HACKERS TARGET US MEDICAL TECH COMPANY

Minnesota's experience could happen in any state. The United States has close to 170,000 drinking water and wastewater systems. Many now connect physical equipment to internet-enabled technology so workers can monitor facilities from a distance. That remote access helps utilities manage equipment spread across wide service areas. However, it may also give an attacker a route into vital controls when operators fail to secure the connection.

Smaller communities often face the greatest challenge. The Government Accountability Office says water systems have widely different cybersecurity capabilities. Many also use older technology that can be difficult to update. At the same time, utilities must stretch limited budgets across essential repairs and regulatory requirements. Cybersecurity upgrades may compete with work that residents can see, such as replacing aging equipment.

A large utility may employ dedicated security professionals. A small town may rely on plant operators who already handle daily operations and after-hours problems. As a result, the communities with fewer resources may also have less ability to monitor suspicious activity around the clock.

Foreign governments have already shown interest in those weak spots. CyberGuy previously reported how Chinese hackers gained access to critical American systems, including infrastructure connected to water and energy. The attacker may change. The underlying weakness often looks familiar: exposed equipment, outdated technology or remote access that lacks strong protection.

A cyberattack against a water utility does not automatically mean the water has been contaminated. In Minnesota, officials reported no known impact on drinking water quality. They also told residents in publicly identified communities that normal water use could continue.

However, a successful attack can cause more serious consequences. The EPA warns that hackers could disrupt treatment or damage equipment. In a worst-case situation, attackers might also interfere with processes that protect water quality.

Manual operations can provide an important safety net. Minnesota workers used those procedures to keep systems running while investigators examined affected technology. Still, a manual backup only helps when employees know how to use it. Utilities need to test those procedures before screens go dark and alarms stop reporting correctly.

CISA published new international guidance on July 28 called "CI Fortify: Advice for Isolating Vital Systems." The guidance urges critical infrastructure operators to separate vital operational technology from less trusted networks. That isolation can help an essential service continue operating when another part of the organization becomes compromised.

CISA released the guidance on the same day MNIT publicly announced the statewide attack. However, the agency has not said it created the document in response to Minnesota. For water utilities, stronger protection may begin with removing unnecessary internet exposure. When remote access remains necessary, CISA advises placing security controls in front of programmable controllers.

Utilities should also change factory passwords and give employees separate login credentials. EPA inspectors have found water systems that continued using default passwords. Inspectors also discovered shared staff accounts or access that remained active after employees left.

Another EPA finding needs careful context. The agency says more than 70% of inspected systems violated basic federal risk assessment or emergency response planning requirements. That figure does not mean 70% had confirmed cybersecurity breaches. However, inspectors found serious digital security weaknesses at some of those facilities.

TRUMP REJECTS IRAN BLAME FOR MINNESOTA CYBERATTACK, POINTS FINGER AT 'CORRUPT' POLITICAL FOE

Residents cannot secure a municipal treatment plant themselves. However, a few steps can help you receive reliable information and avoid scams during an incident.

Check your city, county health department or water utility website for updates. Officials will tell you whether you need to reduce water use or boil tap water. Avoid making decisions based on an unverified neighborhood post.

A cyberattack may affect communications or automated equipment without changing water quality. Continue normal use unless local officials provide different instructions. However, follow any boil-water notice immediately if one appears.

Your city may use text messages, automated calls or government phone alerts during a service disruption. Take a moment to check the emergency alert settings on your iPhone or Android. Also, sign up for your city's local notification system if one is available.

A backup supply can help during any water interruption, whether it begins with a cyberattack or equipment failure. The CDC recommends storing at least one gallon of water per person each day for three days. Households may need more for pets or people with medical needs.

Scammers often take advantage of outages and breaking news. You may receive a message claiming that your water bill failed or that your service will be disconnected. Another message may offer bottled water assistance through a payment link. Do not use the phone number or link inside an unexpected message. Instead, contact the utility through its official website or the number printed on your bill. CyberGuy has also explained how scammers impersonate water and other utility companies by spoofing familiar phone numbers.

Minnesota contained a troubling attack without a known drinking water emergency. Workers restored Braham's plant while other utilities relied on manual controls or contingency procedures. However, the number of systems targeted should get the attention of every governor and mayor in America. Hackers apparently found a way to reach dozens of local utilities during the same two-day period. The preliminary suspicion involving Iranian hackers also raises the stakes. Still, investigators need more evidence before anyone treats that attribution as settled. Every community should know which water controls face the internet and whether workers can operate essential equipment manually. States should also help smaller towns that cannot afford their own cybersecurity teams.

How confident are you that your community could handle a cyberattack on its water system, and what would you want local officials to tell you first? Let us know by writing to us at CyberGuy.com.

item.title: Haunting new images reveal the final ship where explorer Sir Ernest Shackleton died
item.description: The first close-up images reveal the remains of Quest in the Labrador Sea, where the historic shipwreck is covered with pink corals, surrounded by marine life and draped in fishing nets.
item.content:encoded:
Officials have released the first close-up images of the remains of Quest, the final ship of the legendary Antarctic explorer Sir Ernest Shackleton.

The images were taken at the ship's location in the Labrador Sea, around 1,280 feet deep in the waters off of Newfoundland and Labrador, Canada, and were released in July. 

After 60 years, the vessel remains recognizable and in moderate condition, Dwight Coleman, co-chief scientist at Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution (WHOI), told Fox News Digital.

MYSTERY OF GOLD COIN SHIPWRECK FINALLY UNMASKED AFTER 30 YEARS: 'FANTASTIC CONCLUSION'

"You could tell it was a ship," he said. "It had an obvious bow and stern, rudder and propeller.

"Even though it was sort of covered in fishing nets, you could still tell that some of that structure was preserved underneath the nets."

In a statement from the Royal Canadian Geographical Society (RCGS), in partnership with WHOI, officials said the wreck "was populated with pink corals, and several species of fish including cod, red fish and wolf fish."

The images show fishing nets draped across parts of the wreck, as well as parts of its metal superstructure and portholes that still remain intact.

Shackleton, one of history's most celebrated Antarctic explorers, died on Quest in 1922 at age 47. He suffered a heart attack while the ship was anchored in South Georgia, a remote island in the South Atlantic. 

'SPECTACULAR' SHIPWRECK FOUND WITH UNDERWATER TIME CAPSULE OF UNTOUCHED CARGO: 'AMAZING FIND'

After his death, Quest was later sold to Norwegian owners. It spent decades sailing in Arctic waters before being crushed by ice floes and sinking in the Labrador Sea in 1962.

John Geiger, CEO of the RCGS, described seeing Quest for the first time as "a moving experience."

"To see Shackleton's ship, and to think that Shackleton was standing on that deck a century ago ... At first, there was a lot of darkness, but suddenly the bow emerges as you are going toward it. It's incredible," Geiger said in a press release.

UNDERWATER ROBOTICS EXPERT REVEALS 'SHIPWRECK CITY' HIDING BENEATH MAJOR URBAN LAKE

The team used WHOI's Falcon ROV to image the ship and create its digital twin, as well as DSV Alvin, the iconic submersible that first visited the Titanic wreck 40 years ago. The vessels were made available through the National Science Foundation.

Coleman of WHOI, who is based in Rhode Island, said a major part of his job was creating a digital twin of the shipwreck.

The ocean scientist said he was surprised to find the wreck covered in fishing nets and teeming with marine life.

"I wasn't expecting all the fishing gear, the nets and all the fish," he said. "I was honestly thinking it was a little bit deeper and in cold water, and that it would be pretty well-preserved and free of fishing gear because I didn't think there was that much fishing up there."

CENTURIES-OLD PIRATE MYSTERY DEEPENS AFTER WRECKS ARE FOUND NEAR BAHAMAS HAVEN

Added Coleman, "Boy, was I wrong. … It was a vibrant sort of marine life ecosystem around it."

While much of the ship remains recognizable, Coleman said its wooden components are "rapidly deteriorating" after decades in the underwater environment.

"A lot of the wood was collapsing and degrading. The wooden deck was basically completely gone," he said.

"The metal structures of the ship were still pretty well intact, although deteriorating."

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER

Coleman said researchers hope to preserve the wreck through detailed digital mapping rather than artifact recovery.

"We understand most of the components that we could find on it, so you're not really learning anything about history by recovering the artifacts. … There really isn't much need to," he said.

Expeditions like this help researchers better understand both maritime history and the marine ecosystems around historic shipwrecks, he added.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE NEWS

"By studying them, we can bring recognition to history and oceanography," Coleman said. "These shipwrecks are now artificial reefs that support diverse sorts of biological communities."

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

He added, "We care about those communities. We want to understand how animals live in the deep ocean. So by bringing this project to the public, the public can gain a deeper appreciation for history and for the ocean."

The newly released images come not long after another Shackleton-linked discovery garnered international attention.

In October 2025, researchers challenged the long-held belief that Shackleton's famed expedition ship Endurance sank solely because it was crushed by Antarctic ice. They argued instead that structural flaws in the vessel also contributed to its loss.

item.content:encoded:
Total Nonstop Action Wrestling (TNA) on Monday confirmed the departures of two wrestlers in its Knockouts Division.

item.title: Departure of New York Times columnist puts a spotlight on the void of pro-Trump voices in its opinion pages
item.description: Ross Douthat's departure to CBS leaves The New York Times with 12 opinion columnists, only two of whom identify as conservative — and were both Kamala Harris voters.
item.content:encoded:
The paper of record doesn't have a representative for roughly half of the U.S. voting population — at least on its opinion pages.

The New York Times has 12 featured columnists following the departure of its longtime conservative writer Ross Douthat, who was poached by CBS News editor-in-chief Bari Weiss last week as a new "60 Minutes" correspondent.

According to a drop-down menu on the Times' homepage, the remaining columnists are Jamelle Bouie, Maureen Dowd, David French, Thomas Friedman, M. Gessen, Michelle Goldberg, Ezra Klein, Nicholas Kristof, Carlos Lozada, Tressie McMillan Cottom, Lydia Polgreen and Bret Stephens.

NYT COLUMNIST SAYS SHE 'DEEPLY' REGRETS PRAISING SENATE HOPEFUL AFTER RAPE ALLEGATION

Of the Times' 12 columnists, only two of them, David French and Bret Stephens, are self-described conservatives but have spent the past decade opposing President Donald Trump, so much so that they both declared their support for Kamala Harris in the 2024 election.

Douthat's new boss, notably, was formerly a Times colleague of his. Weiss resigned from the Gray Lady as an opinion editor in 2020 after being ostracized and bullied by far-left staffers, famously declaring at the time that "Twitter has become [the Times'] ultimate editor." 

Her resignation followed the debacle at the paper after publishing the now-infamous Tom Cotton op-ed in 2020 about using federal troops to quell civil unrest. That prompted a volcanic social media revolt from liberal Times employees and the ousting of multiple opinion staffers in one of the most embarrassing episodes in the paper's recent history.

NYT COLUMNIST 'TORN' ABOUT ROOTING FOR IRANIAN REGIME'S DOWNFALL SINCE IT WOULD GIVE A WIN TO TRUMP, NETANYAHU

The politics of the remaining Times columnists can be seen in their recent commentary and the controversies they've been swept up in. In April, Thomas Friedman said he found himself "torn" about rooting for the Iranian regime's downfall if it meant it would be a victory for "terrible," "awful human beings" President Donald Trump and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.

In May, Nicholas Kristof sparked an international outcry when he reported without skepticism that Palestinian prisoners detained in Israel were being raped by dogs — Kristof also made an ill-fated bid for Oregon governor in 2021, as a Democrat. 

Last month, Goldberg was forced to walk back her fawning coverage of disgraced Maine Senate candidate Graham Platner after the Democrat was accused of sexual assault.

ISRAELI PM NETANYAHU INITIATING DEFAMATION LAWSUIT AGAINST NEW YORK TIMES OVER CONTROVERSIAL ‘DOG RAPE’ STORY

The overwhelming liberal slant of the Times' opinion pages can also apply to the paper's editorial board, which hasn't endorsed a Republican for president since Dwight D. Eisenhower nearly 70 years ago. In 17 straight elections, it's endorsed the Democratic candidate, including defeated hopefuls like George McGovern, Walter Mondale, Michael Dukakis, John Kerry, Hillary Clinton and Kamala Harris.

Just two days after Trump won the 2024 election, The New York Times published a somber video featuring 10 of its columnists, including Douthat, French and Stephens, all offering their predictions of "the worst version of a Trump administration."

In the video, Polgreen insisted Trump will "fulfill his promise to be a dictator on Day One."

Meanwhile, the opinion pages at The Washington Post have had quite the makeover. Its owner, Jeff Bezos, quashed its planned endorsement of Harris and implemented an edict for its opinion section to promote "personal liberties and free markets," prompting major backlash from liberal critics.

"Our readers are overwhelmingly liberal, right?" Washington Post opinion editor Adam O'Neal told Fox News Digital last year, who announced last week he is leaving The Post at the end of August. "And they're all overwhelmingly located in blue states. And just a few blue states. And they're over-represented on the coasts. And so, one way to look at it would be to say, 'Well, if you're non-partisan, and you have a highly partisan readership, they may be offended by that.' And maybe that's true. But looking forward as I rebuild, I really just see it as an opportunity to expand our reach."

But with Douthat's departure from the Times, the conservative representation in its opinion pages becomes even smaller — and what little remains is fervently anti-Trump.

The New York Times did not respond to Fox News Digital's requests for comment.

item.title: Steelers defend Aaron Rodgers' right to voice opinions after ESPN Fauci segment
item.description: The Pittsburgh Steelers defended Aaron Rodgers' right to voice his opinion after his ESPN segment about Anthony Fauci sparked social media backlash.
item.content:encoded:
The Aaron Rodgers segment on ESPN got folks on both sides of the Anthony Fauci debate quite riled up on Monday.

People got angry at ESPN — some for allowing Rodgers on air at all, and others because he was steered away from discussing the Dianna Russini and Mike Vrabel scandal on air.

Some people defended Rodgers for calling out Fauci for pleading the Fifth Amendment 111 times during recent U.S. Senate hearings.

AARON RODGERS EVISCERATES ANTHONY FAUCI AFTER PLEADING THE FIFTH AT SENATE HEARING: 'ABSOLUTE CRIMINAL'

And others attacked Rodgers for lying about his COVID-19 vaccine status or otherwise just not agreeing with their viewpoint.

The segment on "The Pat McAfee Show" left no safe space for anyone, including the "progrum" itself.

The issue became so fiery on social media that the Pittsburgh Steelers felt the need to address the situation.

So, the club is defending Rodgers and his right to voice his opinion.

"Discussions around culture and politics can bring differing perspectives, and our players are entitled to their own personal views," Steelers spokesman Burt Lauten said in a statement to Fox News Digital/OutKick.

"With respect to that, I am certain there are a variety of opinions on many topics within our locker room."

It appears the Steelers believe that people, including their players, have a right to their own opinions.

Imagine that. It's as if the Steelers are located in America and have read the U.S. Constitution.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

Chalk one up for freedom of expression. And chalk one up for the Steelers, which have been notably consistent in this manner in the past.

You'll recall in May 2025, Mason Rudolph, another Steelers quarterback, incited online approval as well as backlash for having the nerve to appear with Vietnam War veteran and former Steelers running back Rocky Bleier and President Donald Trump at a rally at the U.S. Steel's Irvin Works plant in West Mifflin, Pennsylvania.

Trump welcomed Rudolph on stage and predicted big things for the player, saying, "He's going to be the guy."

Fans went nuts.

MAGA immediately rallied to Rudolph and bought more jerseys than any backup quarterback has a right to sell.

Socialists, Democrats, liberals, progressives, communists, including the Viet Cong, people who hate puppies, anarchists, and perhaps Iran (kidding) despised the moment as an utter betrayal of the Steelers' six Super Bowl titles and the Terrible Towel.

The Steelers themselves, meanwhile, reacted with aplomb. With sanity. With class.

"Our alumni and current players make their own individual decisions and these do not necessarily reflect the views of the Pittsburgh Steelers organization," the club said in an email to fans who complained.

And now, with this Rodgers appearance, the club is sticking to its practice of acknowledging viral public reaction, defending its players' right to an opinion, and not really taking a side.

This is more than good public relations. It's public good policy.

The Steelers recognize that their locker room is a melting pot of races, religions, ideas, and opinions. And no one representing any one cause is more respected or heard than anyone else by the organization.

Rodgers undoubtedly has the team's loudest megaphone. And he uses it quite deftly to relay his opinions. So it would be counterproductive for the Steelers to in any way kneecap that or him.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE SPORTS COVERAGE ON FOXNEWS.COM

But it would also be counterproductive to wholly agree with Rodgers because that could alienate other players.

So, the club is going to do what is best for club peace – which in this case comes with the added advantage of being the right thing to do.

item.title: WWE star Brie Bella says she'll be 'out for a bit' after suffering broken scapula during SummerSlam match
item.description: Brie Bella revealed she broke her scapula during her SummerSlam six-woman tag team match but somehow finished the bout before heading to the hospital.
item.content:encoded:
WWE star Brie Bella announced Monday she will be "out for a bit" after suffering a broken scapula during her six-woman tag team match at SummerSlam over the weekend.

Bella made the revelation in a post on her Instagram account and thanked fans for their outpouring of support.

COMPLETE PRO WRESTLING COVERAGE ON FOX NEWS DIGITAL

"I wanted to thank you all for sending me all the love, warm wishes and prayers," she wrote. "When I was sitting in the hospital, I was reading everything you guys were sending my way, love you all!!! Unfortunately I’ll be out for a bit. I broke my scapula. If there’s one thing I know about my sister and I is that we don’t let broken bones stop us. Not sure how I finished that match, but I do believe between the adrenaline, passion for the business and the love for all the women I work with, it gave me the drive to finish.

"Now my new journey starts!! Buddy said he’s going to be my assistant, Birdie‘s going to be my nurse and they both told me that daddy is going to be my personal chef, so I am set!! if there is one thing I know about Brie Mode, she always finds a way to come back to her wrestling home. Let the recovery begin."

Bella appeared to suffer the injury after taking a move from opponent Jacy Jayne. Bella was seated next to the steel steps when her opponent, Jacy Jayne, hit a running senton on her. At that moment, she began to clutch her shoulder and kept rubbing it during the rest of the match with her sister Nikki Bella and Paige.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE SPORTS COVERAGE ON FOXNEWS.COM

WWE Chief Content Officer Paul "Triple H" Levesque told reporters after Night 1 that the injury "seems pretty bad."

"Yeah, she’s injured," he said. "I don’t have an update yet. We’ve taken her. She was here, got some treatment done here, has been taken to the hospital to get some scans done. Don’t have a clean answer on it yet.

"I know she hurt her shoulder. It seems pretty bad, but I don’t have an answer yet. Hopefully we will soon. Hopefully, it won’t be as bad as we thought it was, but that’s the nature of the game."

The Bellas and Paige teamed up against Jayne, Lainey Reid and Fallon Henley. Jayne scored the pinfall over Paige to give her team the win.

Brie Bella made her stunning return to WWE at the Royal Rumble in January and then was set to team with her sister at WrestleMania 42 before Nikki Bella suffered her own injury.

Instead, she teamed with Paige as they won the WWE Women’s Tag Team Championship.

Now, Brie will be on the shelf for the time being while Nikki eyes singles gold.

item.title: New stars, fading appeal: Has the Hollywood Walk of Fame lost its luster?
item.description: Historians say the Hollywood Walk of Fame has lost its luster amid cracked stars, aggressive vendors and a boulevard that feels far from glamorous.
item.content:encoded:
Even as new inductees arrive, some Tinseltown historians say the legendary Hollywood Walk of Fame has lost its luster.

The iconic strip that began with a groundbreaking ceremony in 1960 and now spans 15 blocks of Hollywood Boulevard and three blocks of Vine Street has experienced physical neglect.

Many of the 2,852 five-pointed brass and terrazzo stars honoring entertainment industry achievements are dirty, cracked and covered in grime. They sit in Hollywood’s commercial center full of discount souvenir shops, panhandlers and pushy vendors. Trash and unpleasant odors are common, while the general overall condition of the boulevard leaves the area feeling neglected and far from glamorous.

CHRISTIAN SLATER OPENS UP ABOUT ‘WEIRD’ REALITY OF FAME AFTER 5 DECADES IN HOLLYWOOD

"It’s really tough today because of what Hollywood has become… there’s very aggressive people on the street," author and pop culture historian Chris Epting told Fox News Digital. "Unfortunately, Hollywood’s been allowed to fall into a really sad state. It’s outright dangerous in many parts."

Epting, who remembers going to the Walk of Fame as far back as the 1970s when he was a kid, noted that when Hollywood as a place began falling apart, it took the Walk of Fame right along with it.

"There’s no way to separate the two," he added. "I think a lot of people lament the fact that part of Hollywood — really most of Hollywood — is not that friendly or inviting the way it once was and the stars on the sidewalk pay that price as well."

Epting, who co-authored the 2017 memoir "Change of Seasons: A Memoir" with musician John Oates of the R&B band Hall & Oates, recalled being with Oates the day he and Hall received their star right in front of the Musicians Institute.

"It’s kind of cool to be part of their little world, the day they got theirs," Epting said, noting that sometimes stars are put in certain places on the famous walkway. For instance, Jay Leno requested that his star be placed at the exact corner where he had twice been arrested for vagrancy early in his comedy career.

"I don’t think many people go out looking for it like they used to, but I think that if they could help the area out a little bit, that would probably help people reconnect with the Walk."

Meanwhile, new inductees are named by the Walk of Fame Selection Committee with roughly 33 honorees selected each year from hundreds of submissions.

Last month, Actress Ming-Na Wen and singer/songwriter Sheila E., both Walk of Famers, joined Hollywood Chamber of Commerce President and CEO Ron Frierson, to announce the Class of 2027 honorees from Funko Hollywood retail store.

AVRIL LAVIGNE HONORED WITH A STAR ON THE HOLLYWOOD WALK OF FAME: ‘I FEEL VERY BLESSED AND GRATEFUL’

Among the new group of entertainment professionals chosen from the overall categories of Motion Pictures, Television, Live Theatre/Live Performance, Radio, Recording, and Sports Entertainment include actors Idris Elba, Sam Elliott, sisters Elle and Dakota Fanning and Kate Hudson.

Netflix CEO Ted Sarandos rounded out the Motion Pictures category, while actors David Alan Grier, Lisa Kudrow, Pedro Pascal and Adam Scott were among those selected in the TV category. Waylon Jennings (posthumously), The Ramones, Smashing Pumpkins and others made the cut in the Recording category.

The full list can be seen here.

"… These 32 extraordinary individuals have each made a lasting impact on audiences around the world through their talent, creativity, and dedication to their craft," Walk of Fame Selection Chairman Peter Roth said in a statement. "We are honored to recognize their remarkable contributions and look forward to celebrating them as they take their place in Hollywood history."

According to the Hollywood Chamber of Commerce, the Hollywood Walk of Fame attracts an estimated 10 million visitors annually. More recent mobility data, however, has the estimate closer to 5 to 6 million visitors each year.

Still, Hollywood historian and storyteller Scott Michaels, known for creating Dearly Departed Tours, an LA tour company that looks at the dark side of Hollywood history, blames much of the Walk of Fame’s decline on the Hollywood Chamber of Commerce, arguing its focus has shifted toward revenue rather than preservation.

Michaels, who was a member of the Chamber for a few years, noted that these days it costs $85,000 to receive a star on the celebrity promenade, while at one time the price tag was just $2,000.

Now, many star ceremonies, which still draw crowds, are scheduled to purposefully coincide with their latest movie or album release. And even corporate brands can receive stars on the Walk.

And because stars are considered historic landmarks never to be removed, certain disgraced figures or minor reality TV names permanently remain.

"There was a time when the Hollywood Walk of Fame was a true honor," Michaels told Fox News Digital, noting that stepping just below the famous celebrity hands and footprints at Grauman’s Chinese Theatre, visitors once experienced the shiny brass-and-terrazzo stars embedded in the sidewalk outside.

Since then, a large silver statue called "The Four Ladies" marking the beginning of the Walk of Fame at the corner of LaBrea and Hollywood Boulevard saw the small bronze of Marilyn Monroe at the very top of it stolen (after a thief sawed it off and took it). Marilyn was recovered, but Michaels noted six years later it’s never been reinstalled.

In August 2025, a van slammed into the statue of the "four trailblazing ladies of color" and heavily damaged pioneering actress Anna May Wong, known as the first Chinese American movie star.

A year later, the damaged likeness of Wong has yet to be fully restored.

While the Chamber may not necessarily be responsible for the statue, it likely had its cooperation on design and approval, Michaels said.

The statue is the "gateway" to the Walk of Fame with tourists often posing in front of it.

Fox News Digital reached out to the Hollywood Chamber of Commerce multiple times for comment.

The 1.3 mile famous boulevard has also generated negative headlines in recent years, including the time actress/singer Miley Cyrus claimed she landed in the hospital with a brutal infection after filming a scene on the Walk of Fame. Another incident involved a homeless man dumping a bucket of feces on a woman’s head.

A few years back, when Michaels petitioned to move Marilyn Monroe’s star from in front of the McDonald’s a few blocks from Grauman’s Chinese Theatre to in front of the theater because he was "sick of seeing her star being covered in s---, piss and trash," his request fell on deaf ears.

Michaels said the Chamber representative’s response was simply, "Who will pay for it?"

'EXORCIST' STAR LINDA BLAIR 'UNKNOWINGLY' WALKED AWAY FROM HOLLYWOOD

Yet, Michaels noted, well over 100 images of Monroe are plastered in shops, on shirts and signs, all visible from the street.

"Vendors are out of control. You can now sell dry fetid sausages without a food grade or inspection, in front of actual licensed restaurants. But try to open a restaurant," Michaels quipped, about the state of the boulevard.

Chuck Suhayda, former board member of the Hollywood Neighborhood Council, told Fox News Digital there was a time when a lot of money was spent keeping the Walk clean and up to date on repairs. He credited that to the Chamber’s Economic Workforce Development department, various agencies like the Hollywood Boulevard Commercial and Entertainment District and "the very effective Community Redevelopment Agency installed in Hollywood under previous California Gov. Jerry Brown."

MASKED BURGLARY CREWS TERRORIZING RITZY NEIGHBORHOODS SHOW 'THEY'RE DOING THEIR HOMEWORK,' VETERAN COP WARNS

Suhayda recalled that historically, security firm Andrews International provided the local Business Improvement District security patrol services on Hollywood Boulevard.

"Cameras were all up and down Hollywood Blvd," Suhayda said, noting that Hollywood is and has been considered "ground zero" for terrorist attacks in an area that extends from the 101 freeway to La Brea Avenue.

Yet, despite the decline, Epting still holds fondness for the iconic boulevard in his heart.

"I was always curious about what celebs were actually there when their star was unveiled," he said, recalling a time in the late ‘80s when he took his visiting aunt from New York to see the famous promenade and wound up seeing a real-life star too.

"She kept saying that along with the stars she wanted to see a celeb too," Epting recalled. "And I said, ‘Well, that’s the last place in the world you would ever go see celebrities’."

"So we’re crossing the street by the Chinese Theater as I say, ‘Aunt Lee, for the last time, you don’t see celebrities come to Hollywood!’ And then a head turns around of a gentleman passing us, and he goes, ‘Well, I don’t know if that’s altogether accurate young man’ and it was Jack Lemmon."

"We both laughed, and it was this charming little moment between sort of all three of us," he recalled.

"But that said, I do hope they figure out a way to make the area more accommodating, more inviting and more engaging because the Walk is, you know, it’s a nice bit of history… it’s kind of like the Hollywood sign. It may just be a sign, but it’s there for so long. It does get sort of engrained in your brain, just like those coral-colored stars on the boulevard."

item.title: MARK PENN: Socialist Mamdani sold a tax on billionaires. Regulars homeowners could pay the price
item.description: The pied-a-terre tax targets far more than billionaires, potentially hitting nearly 1 million New York City homeowners and crashing condo prices.
item.content:encoded:
It sounded simple and even kind of warmly populist in nature — a small tax on "pied-à-terre" properties in New York City. But the more you dig into it, as with all things from Mayor Zohran Mamdani, the more you see it as part of a far more devious plan that could destabilize the New York City housing market and cost middle-class people their homes and savings.

Gotta love whoever pulled this French name into implying the tax would just fall on a few very rich people — no more than 31,000. That was pure deception.

Think about it for a moment: Why tax nonresident property owners? Because they don’t vote in the city. By design, the policy targets non-resident property owners who lack a vote in local elections, shifting municipal tax burdens onto individuals who have no direct voice at the ballot box. And then the city uses money extracted from non-voting property owners to plug general budget deficits and fund broader municipal initiatives. Who knows – perhaps the money will even wind up funding residents who are in New York City illegally.

MAMDANI EXTENDS DEADLINE FOR NYC HOMEOWNERS TO SEEK EXEMPTION FROM NEW PIED-À-TERRE TAX

Because the Department of Finance’s initial roll sent notices to 960,000 property entries, primary residents are now forced to navigate bureaucratic hurdles to prove their exemption. The statute had a little-noticed provision that co-ops and condos qualify for the tax if the NYC Department of Finance computers identify their assessed value over $1 million. Presto chango — hundreds of thousands of New York homeowners were caught up in the initial mailing. And the surcharge on non-primary residences can reach up to 5% or more of market value annually.

So now add $50,000 a year in costs to a million-dollar non-primary condo. What are those owners going to do? Hit the sell, sell, sell button.  Imposing steep surcharges on secondary condo owners could chill the broader housing market, reduce demand from out-of-town buyers and ultimately drag down property values across the board. In the end, local homeowners will pay the price through diminished equity. It’s simple economics.

And if you do live in NYC as a primary resident, you now have to prove it. Because the city did not properly screen out existing voters or primary taxpayers beforehand, they are making residents file documents such as their federal tax returns just to clear their names. If you live elsewhere in New York State but keep a place in the city, or if you own two apartments in the city, you are also caught in this net.

LIBERAL PODCASTER SAYS HE WAS 'DOXED' BY MAMDANI'S 'WANTED POSTER' OF PROPERTY OWNERS

And never mind that out-of-town property holders were already paying taxes here even though they use few if any city services. No use of schools, no clogging of traffic, reduced sanitation. They would have an argument to be taxed less, not more. And perhaps they can go to court arguing that the tax is discriminatory since it applies to a class of people without a rational basis related to municipal service usage. It potentially violates the equal protection and commerce clauses.

CLINTON, OBAMA-ERA DEMOCRATIC HEAVYWEIGHTS PENN AND EMANUEL RIP NYC'S MAMDANI OVER TAXES, ISRAEL, BLAST DSA

CLICK HERE FOR MORE FOX NEWS OPINION

This is how creeping socialism works: Politicians advertise that they are going after only those greedy out-of-town billionaires, while creating a sprawling administrative property database that exposes personal details of thousands of everyday homeowners and forces residents to surrender tax returns just to defend their homes.

 And before you know it, what was billed as "tax the rich" hits you and your family.

item.title: Popular weight-loss drugs may help protect against a deadly disease, doctor says
item.description: A breast cancer surgeon explains how GLP-1 drugs like Ozempic and Wegovy may lower cancer recurrence risk by reducing BMI, estrogen and inflammation.
item.content:encoded:
GLP-1 medications have transformed diabetes and obesity treatment, but emerging research suggests their benefits could extend far beyond those purposes — potentially even aiding in cancer prevention and survival.

Dr. Loren Rourke, a Texas-based board-certified breast cancer surgeon, author and speaker, said growing research suggests glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) medications — including Ozempic and Wegovy — may be associated with a lower risk of cancer diagnoses and recurrence. 

She pointed to findings presented at the 2026 American Society of Clinical Oncology (ASCO) Annual Meeting in Chicago, where researchers reported an association between GLP-1 use and lower breast cancer recurrence rates, as well as a potential role in preventing the disease.

MILLIONS COULD GAIN EASIER ACCESS TO POPULAR PEPTIDES AFTER FDA PANEL VOTE

However, she noted that the evidence remains observational and can’t prove that the drugs reduce cancer risk.

"So these aren’t studies that, unfortunately, patients can latch onto, call their doctor and say, ‘I want to get on a GLP-1 right now to reduce my risk of breast cancer or make my breast cancer better,’" Rourke told Fox News Digital. "However, what it did do was shine the light on GLP-1s and that relationship."

The main reason that GLP-1s may aid in cancer prevention, according to Rourke, is that the drugs promote weight loss and reduce chronic inflammation.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER

"GLP-1s cause a decrease in your BMI. They cause weight reduction," she told Fox News Digital. "We know that a lower BMI equals a better prognosis with breast cancer."

"So if the secondary effect of taking a GLP-1 means you’re going to lose weight, then that’s a benefit, because we know you’re going to do better with breast cancer."

Diabetes and obesity medications can also lower estrogen production associated with excess body fat, the surgeon noted.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES

"The more fat you have, the higher your estrogen production," Rourke said. "You’re kind of bathing your body in estrogen, so to speak. So it intuitively makes sense that we are seeing this correlation or association."

GLP-1s also decrease the inflammatory state in which cancer thrives, the surgeon noted.

"So if it’s fixing the overall chronic inflammation of the body, that’s going to help for a lot of reasons," she said.

"I think this is going to extend beyond breast cancer, but we need to get that scientific proof of a direct cause — is this just an association or a correlation?"

Rourke emphasized that researchers have not yet proven that GLP-1 medications directly affect breast cancer cells.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

"But this study has now garnered enough attention, interest and scientific hypotheses that the work is getting started for the randomized controlled trials that we’re all waiting for — and then we can act upon those."

To patients who are considering starting GLP-1s, Rourke offered the following advice.

"My bottom-line message on this one is, if you have an elevated BMI, you’re trying to lose weight, you’ve tried a healthy diet, you’ve tried to exercise, and you’re not winning that fight, consider GLP-1s, and you’re going to get a secondary benefit."

In particular, post-menopausal women who are struggling with weight gain could get an extra benefit, Rourke added, but she urges them to "call their doctor and have that one-on-one conversation."

item.title: WATCH: GOP senator unloads on 'creature of Washington' challenger in critical Senate showdown
item.description: Jon Husted says Sherrod Brown's 32 years in Washington produced nothing but higher energy prices and liberal votes out of step with Ohio voters.
item.content:encoded:
MARYSVILLE, OH - The Ohio Senate race could very well decide the balance of power in the U.S. Senate in November and incumbent Republican Jon Husted is making the case that the reasons his Democratic opponent was voted out of office two years ago are still relevant today.

"He’s spent 32 years in Washington, and he's got nothing to show for it, the voters over here in Ohio know it," Husted told Fox News Digital at the annual Summer Farm Fest on Sunday when asked about his race against former Democratic Sen. Sherrod Brown.

"That's why they sent him packing two years ago. He was defeated by Bernie Moreno by over 200,000 votes. This is all he's done. He's been in an elected office since 1974. He hasn't done anything in the private sector. He's just been a creature of Washington and I think the voters finally are tired of it. That's why they sent him packing. I don't think they're gonna have any enthusiasm for rehiring him for a job that he failed at."

After representing Ohio in the Senate for almost two decades after years of serving in the House of Representatives, Brown was defeated by Republican Bernie Moreno in 2024 in a blistering campaign that was one of the most expensive in U.S. history. Moreno consistently tied Brown to the unpopular positions of then-President Joe Biden, and Husted told Fox News Digital those concerns still exist, particularly on immigration.

FOX NEWS POLL: COOL YOUR SERVERS! VOTERS REJECT DATA CENTERS

"We had basically an invasion of 11 million people," Husted said. "He supported amnesty for them. He supported Social Security payments for illegals, healthcare for illegals, COVID checks for illegals. The sanctuary cities he supported led to crime, fentanyl, human trafficking in our state, and it's been terrible, and the voters know this."

"They know that he failed them. They know when he goes off to Washington with his comrades that he votes like a liberal, that he's too liberal for Ohio, that he has a track record of voting with Bernie Sanders and Kamala Harris and Joe Biden, and that's out of step with where Ohio is."

Over the last few weeks, Brown has blanketed the airwaves with ads criticizing Husted on data centers, a hot-button issue in Ohio, arguing that Husted’s support of data centers over the years has resulted in higher energy prices for consumers.

Husted, who was appointed to the Senate in January 2025 after the departure of now-Vice President JD Vance, pushed back on that assertion when asked about the ads.

"He had 32 years in Congress, he did nothing about it, and I, in my, just briefly over a year there, have legislation to require data centers to build their own power, to pay their own way, and to give the benefits of their presence to the citizens of those local communities, rather than the way that Sherrod Brown has done it, where he's failed," Husted explained.

DEM SENATE CANDIDATE SHERROD BROWN CLAIMS HE SUPPORTS 'CLOSING THE BORDER'; GOP SAYS RECORD PROVES OTHERWISE

Husted continued, "This is the problem with the guy, is that he does nothing, and then a problem comes out, and he says, blame that person… He didn't do anything about it. He never does anything about it. He just waits for problems to happen. And then he says, well, it's the other person's fault. It's time to hold him accountable."

Husted made the case that the policies Brown supported in Congress led to the high energy rates the country is seeing now.

"He spent 32 years in Washington and didn't do anything except raise our electricity prices because he and the radical climate change agenda shut 23 power plants in Ohio," Husted said. "If we had those 23 power plants today, we wouldn't have high energy prices."

Husted continued, "Him voting for Obamacare, which has doubled the price of health care insurance in the state of Ohio and around the country. He needs to be held to account for his failed policies."

While Ohio has historically been known as a bellwether swing state, President Donald Trump won the state convincingly in 2016, 2020 and 2024, shifting the Buckeye State to a reliably red stronghold. However, recent polling, including a Fox News poll in June, shows Husted trailing Brown as Republicans battle the historical headwinds of the party in power struggling in midterm elections.

Brown, recruited back into politics in part by Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer, is looking to flip one of the four seats Democrats need to regain control of the Senate, with Ohio among the party's top pickup opportunities alongside Alaska, Maine and North Carolina.

With less than 100 days to go until the midterms, Husted says that Brown’s record will be front and center.

"Just showing the contrast between 32 years of failure from Sherrod Brown and the fact that I'm an Ohio guy, I've fought for Ohioans, I've helped in state government to turn this state in the right direction," Husted said. "We now have more jobs than we've ever had in our state's history, the lowest unemployment rate, frankly, than we ever had in our states' history. And we don't need to send this guy back to Washington, Sherrod Brown, to continue the failed policies that have harmed the country and harmed our state. We need a guy like me who will fight for Ohio."

Fox News Digital reached out to the Brown campaign for comment.

item.title: Former Vikings captain Jack Brewer calls out Lynx coach Cheryl Reeve for 'trans kids belong' shirt
item.description: Jack Brewer slams Cheryl Reeve's "trans kids belong" shirt and calls on WNBA coaches to speak out against what he calls promoting atrocities.
item.content:encoded:
Former Minnesota Vikings captain Jack Brewer witnessed a clash of cultures in his state this past weekend.

Ahead of Sunday's WNBA game between the Minnesota Lynx and Indiana Fever, the third organized rally in support of Sophie Cunningham's support for protecting women's sports pitted women's rights activists against pro-trans counter-protesters outside the Target Center.

Inside the arena, Lynx head coach Cheryl Reeve was seen wearing a shirt that read "trans kids belong."

CHERYL REEVE SENDS CLEAR MESSAGE TO SOPHIE CUNNINGHAM WITH ‘TRANS KIDS BELONG’ SHIRT DURING FEVER-LYNX GAME

Brewer disagreed with Reeve's shirt.

"The Lynx have a rich history in that state. That team was established the year I got to Minnesota, and I remember watching them. To now see a coach representing that team in this way is sad. It is sad to think that young girls in Minnesota are coming to games and watching teams promote something like that. It is ridiculous to think that a grown woman would go so hard in support of men playing against women and entering women’s locker rooms," Brewer said in a statement provided to Fox News Digital.

"This coach is promoting the idea that children who should be receiving psychiatric treatment... should instead be affirmed. It is disgusting and sad. These people are sick and need help. We should be praying for them and finding treatment for them. Instead, people like this coach in Minnesota are promoting these types of atrocities. It is a terrible thing."

Brewer added that the visual was personal to him as a father, and someone with ties to Minnesota. Brewer began his career with the Vikings in 2002 after playing football at the University of Minnesota from 1998-2001.

"As a father and someone whose family is deeply connected to Minnesota sports, I have an eight-year-old daughter who plays highly competitive tennis and competitive soccer. She also plays and trains in Minnesota. We go to Minnesota during the summers. Her cousins, grandparents, aunts and uncles are there. My nieces and nephews are there. I went to school in Minnesota, my family lives there, and my cousins coach various sports there. I am involved in sports in that state. It is embarrassing," Brewer said.

In addition to Reeve, three other WNBA coaches have come under scrutiny for their responses to questions about women's sports in the last week alone.

Golden State Valkyries coach Natalie Nakase, Indiana Fever coach Stephanie White and Portland Fire coach Alex Sarama all declined to back protecting women's sports at pre-game press conference this past weekend.

STORM CO-OWNER SUSPENDED AFTER INCIDENT WITH SOPHIE CUNNINGHAM FANS AS STAR BREAKS SILENCE ON CONTROVERSY

Meanwhile, Seattle Storm co-owner Celeste Keaton was suspended and fined after allegedly berating two young Cunningham fans who were sitting courtside for celebrating Cunningham's stance on women's sports.

Brewer sent a message to the WNBA's other leaders with advice on how to proceed.

"My advice to other coaches, owners and teams is to speak the truth. Every coach who loves God, loves this country and wants to protect women needs to speak out against coaches who are that ignorant. You should not be able to promote something like that without being held accountable. You should be held accountable for your actions," he said.

Brewer also criticized the league for its handling of Caitlin Clark.

"They cannot stand up for the white girl, even though the white girl sells more jerseys than the other players in the league. They cannot admit that the white girl is worth protecting. Caitlin Clark should be the face of the WNBA. She should be to the WNBA what Michael Jordan was to the NBA. Caitlin Clark is the reason people watch the WNBA."Her image should become the logo of the WNBA because she is the reason the league has become popular. I remember watching the WNBA in its early stages," Brewer said.

"There was hardly anybody in the crowd, and they had to let people attend for free. Now stadiums are half-full and, in some cases, nearly sold out."It is sad that the league will not fully support its star player because she does not fit the race-and-gender ideology they want to portray through victimhood. She is not a victim, so she does not fit their victimhood mentality. That is why she gets no love from the teams of the WNBA. It is terrible."

Brewer is backing Clark and Cunningham, and hopes the rest of the WNBA and its fans can rally behind them.

"Caitlin Clark’s impact on the WNBA cannot be denied. Caitlin Clark is the Jerry West of the WNBA. They need to make her the logo and emblem of the league, whether they want to agree with it or not. She has defined the game. There will be greater players than Caitlin Clark, just as there have been greater players than Jerry West. But Caitlin Clark, like Jerry West, made the sport popular at this particular time and juncture," he said.

"They need to give this girl her flowers while she is doing it."That is also why Sophie Cunningham is so popular. She is standing up for herself and standing up for Caitlin Clark. I love her for that, and I have her back. I do not care what Black girls, Black men or anyone else has to say. I am a Sophie Cunningham fan. I do not agree with everything about her, and I think she can be too provocative and show her body too much, but I still pray for her. I like that she stands up for herself, and I like that she has Caitlin Clark’s back, because so do I."

item.title: Holy Land battle: Solomon's Pools become flashpoint in fight over Israel's biblical heritage
item.description: Israeli officials say the ancient Solomon's Pools have fallen into disrepair under Palestinian Authority administration, raising concerns over preservation and biblical heritage.
item.content:encoded:
Built more than 2,000 years ago to supply Jerusalem with water, Solomon's Pools have become the center of a modern political dispute, with officials from the nearby Israeli town of Efrat accusing the Palestinian Authority of allowing the historic site to deteriorate after it was placed under Ramallah's jurisdiction following the 1993 Oslo Accords.

Most archaeologists date the construction of Solomon's Pools, three ancient reservoirs located between Efrat and Bethlehem, south of Israel's capital, to the Hasmonean period in the second century B.C. The reservoirs were built to supply water to Jerusalem during the Second Temple period. Herod the Great (37–4 B.C.) later expanded the system to provide water to his palace-fortress at Herodium.

"Solomon's Pools are not only the history of the Jewish people in the Land of Israel and the source of Jerusalem's living water, but also the future of Efrat in our ability to exercise our sovereignty, preserve Efrat's development space and sustain tourism for all religions in the area between Jerusalem and Hebron," Dovi Shefler, mayor of Efrat, told Fox News Digital.

EXCLUSIVE: ISRAELI PRESIDENT HERZOG BLASTS MAMDANI, PRAISES TRUMP, SOUNDS ALARM ON IRAN

The three reservoirs collectively hold approximately 288,000 cubic meters of water, or more than 10 million cubic feet. They are fed by the Arrub and el-Biyar aqueducts, which, together with rainwater, historically supplied Jerusalem with water year-round. During the British Mandate, the pools underwent significant renovations and became known as "Jerusalem's beach" until the Oslo Accords.

Under the agreements, the West Bank was divided into Areas A, B and C. Solomon's Pools are located in Area A, which falls under Palestinian civil and security control.

Yonatan Marcus, chief of staff of the Efrat Municipality, told Fox News Digital that during the negotiations, then-Prime Minister Yitzhak Rabin maintained that the pools would remain under Israeli control, alongside other archaeological sites of major Judeo-Christian significance such as Rachel's Tomb in Bethlehem.

However, during the mapping process, he said, the words "Solomon's Pools" remained within Area C on zoomed-out maps, while the reservoirs themselves ultimately mistakenly fell inside Area A.

TRUMP’S MASSIVE GOP FAITH BLOC RAISES RED FLAG ON IRAN DEAL: TRUST HIM, NOT HIS TEAM

Marcus said under Palestinian Authority control, things changed for the worse. "When you visit today, you can see that the place is neglected. Much of it has been destroyed. There are signs everywhere in Arabic stating that swimming is not permitted because the pools are filled with sewage water," he said.

He added that the sewage contamination was not natural, with wastewater deliberately diverted into the pools, replacing the fresh water that flowed there until the Oslo Accords. He said this occurred despite the PLO's commitment under the agreement to protect historical sites in Area A.

"Our main goal is to protect these magnificent pools. It's not just about Jewish history; it's about Judeo-Christian history and whoever believes in the people of the Bible who walked here," he said.

He described the reservoirs as the largest archaeological pools in Israel, saying they occupy a strategic location between the Western Wall and the Cave of the Patriarchs and Matriarchs along Route 60, known as the Biblical Highway.

Although the pools are located in Area A, Marcus said visits by Israelis take place only on coordinated tours secured by the IDF's Judea and Samaria Division, as permitted under the Oslo Accords.

He noted that visits by Israeli officials, including Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich, have prompted improvements, saying the Palestinian Authority removed about 200 bags of garbage from the site following years of neglect.

CHRISTIAN LEADERS HOLD EMERGENCY SUMMIT IN JERUSALEM TO CONFRONT GLOBAL RISE IN ANTISEMITISM

"If the pressure of our coming here is going to make them take care of the site, then wonderful. In the end, our goal is for it to be preserved," he said.

Ahmad Fattouh, a spokesman for Palestinian Authority President Mahmoud Abbas's Fatah faction, rejected the allegations.

"It's absolutely audacious that the leadership of the colonial settlement of Efrat claims to be concerned about the condition of Burak Sulaymān's pools when they are the very reason behind its declining water levels," Fattouh told Fox News Digital. He said Israeli locals diverted the springs that feed the pools and argued that the Palestinian Authority has restored the site and developed it as a tourist destination.

Fattouh also accused Israeli officials of using the issue to justify taking control of the site, saying Smotrich's visit showed that the pools were not completely dry, contrary to claims by Efrat officials.

Yishai Fleisher, international spokesman for Hebron, said the pools are akin to rediscovering a lost part of the Jewish Temple, as they supplied Jerusalem with water for some 2,000 years.

He said preserving the site begins with attracting visitors, producing educational videos, improving access along the new road from northern Efrat, hosting senior Israeli officials and establishing a permanent presence with cameras, patrols and farms.

"Since the story started breaking, the P.A. is trying to build a mosque there. The goal of the P.A. is to stop Israeli presence in Judea and Samaria and the Land of Israel. They are not about developing anything for its own sake," Fleisher claimed to Fox News Digital.

Fleisher, who is an influential voice among the Israeli right, called for a radical change in policy. "What we really have to do is dismantle the P.A. and assert sovereignty over Judea and Samaria. In the meantime, the line should be redrawn so that Solomon's Pools, which are essentially archaeological sites, are placed under Israeli control in Area C," he said.

item.title: Aaron Rodgers calls out ESPN for ignoring Dianna Russini-Mike Vrabel scandal: 'What are we doing here?'
item.description: Rodgers blasted Russini, questioning how much her alleged relationship with Vrabel has an impact on the NFL during a candid "The Pat McAfee Show" interview.

Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers took his microphone on "The Pat McAfee Show" on Monday and unloaded on Dr. Anthony Fauci and ESPN, the network airing the program, in a diatribe heard ‘round the NFL.

During his evisceration of ESPN, he called out Dianna Russini, a former reporter with the network before joining The Athletic as an NFL insider.

Russini was embroiled in a major scandal this offseason, as she was alleged to have had an inappropriate relationship with New England Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel. Russini resigned from her role at The Athletic, and Vrabel left the Patriots during the NFL Draft to enter counseling as details began to unfold around his relationship with Russini.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE SPORTS COVERAGE ON FOXNEWS.COM

During his diatribe, Rodgers wondered how an alleged affair like the one Russini had with Vrabel could affect the NFL, while simultaneously roasting ESPN for their lack of coverage compared to other media outlets surrounding the scandal.

"Look at what the network’s doing. You have literally an individual that maybe used to work at ESPN, that covers our league at the highest level, and there’s a major scandal," Rodgers told McAfee and his crew. "And it’s just like nobody can f---ing talk about it? Like, what are we doing here?"

One of McAfee’s co-hosts told Rodgers that he of all people should understand how personal lives are meant to be personal, but Rodgers had a retort.

AARON RODGERS EVISCERATES ANTHONY FAUCI AFTER PLEADING THE FIFTH AT SENATE HEARING: 'ABSOLUTE CRIMINAL'

"I understand, but if it’s affecting certain things – if there’s leaks going on, there’s tampering going on," he said. "If that person is also an MVP voter and Coach of the Year voter. Remember when I won MVP in 2021, and that bum in Chicago – yeah, that’s real life. How are we allowing these people to have an impact?

Rodgers joked, "I told these boys I was bringing it today," pointing to likely producers behind the cameras during the live taping at Steelers training camp.

But it was the truth. A simple question about Rodgers’ mindset heading into his final NFL season this year from McAfee led to him mocking Fauci.

"I’ll plead the Fifth," Rodgers said before going scorched Earth on Fauci, whom he was mocking after the former White House COVID advisor invoked the Fifth Amendment 111 times during a Senate hearing last week.

Rodgers, though, also may have a gripe with Russini herself, especially during his time with the New York Jets. It was a failed tenure for the four-time MVP quarterback following years of success with the Green Bay Packers.

During his time in New York, Russini, working for The Athletic at the time, was very active in Jets reporting around the Rodgers turmoil and how the franchise was allegedly being affected by him.

In 2024, The Athletic reported Rodgers wanted to continue playing past that season, but not for the Jets. Rodgers said at the time on McAfee’s show it was "100% false," while ripping into the media.

"There is not a lot of journalistic integrity anymore, I don’t think," Rodgers said, which prompted McAfee to respond by saying, "Standards."

MIKE VRABEL UNTOUCHED BY DIANNA RUSSINI SCANDAL AT FIRST PRESS CONFERENCE OF PATRIOTS TRAINING CAMP

"The standards are what they are," Rodgers replied, while not implicating Russini directly. "Listen, some of the stuff that I’ve read I would say the majority is limited in its truth, and questionable in its content. Meaning, I don’t understand why some of the articles written last year, because it seemed like they were really trying to ruin people’s lives."

Rodgers also mentioned how tight-knit his inner circle is.

"I don’t have anybody, I don’t believe, that is in my inner circle that would spend any time talking to a reporter about other people’s s---, or trying to slam ‘em, or trying to protect themselves," he said. "But, unfortunately, this business has turned into a lot of cover your a--, you know. I guess that’s part of what this is, people trying to cover their a--, so they gotta have a fall guy. It was [former Jets OC Nathaniel] Hackett, it was [former Jets head coach] Robert [Saleh], it was [former Jets GM] Joe [Douglas], then it’s me."

Russini said in 2025 on the "Scoop City" podcast that the Jets gave Rodgers an ultimatum that he won’t be doing interviews on McAfee’s show any longer. Obviously, that didn’t come to fruition.

Rodgers has told ESPN’s top NFL insider, Adam Schefter, to "lose my number" in 2023 when the football world was waiting for his decision on whether he’d retire or not following his darkness retreat. He also noted getting a similar text from Russini, though he didn’t answer. He said if he did, it would’ve been the same answer he gave Schefter.

Russini resigned from her post at The Athletic amid mounting criticism over her relationship with Vrabel after photographs of them hugging and holding hands at a private resort in Sedona, Arizona, went viral. After initially trying to downplay it, saying "reporters interact with sources away from stadiums and other venues," Russini ultimately released her resignation.

After the original photos, others dating back to 2020 showed Vrabel and Russini kissing at a bar in New York City. The pictures exclusively obtained by the New York Post were taken in the early hours of March 11, 2020.

"They were kissing, and they were all over each other," an eyewitness told the outlet. "He had a ring on."

While Russini resigned, Vrabel was back with the Patriots after a counseling visit, which fell on Day 3 of the 2026 NFL Draft.

Vrabel said he had difficult conversations with his family, while also speaking with his players about the situation. The Patriots said before the draft they "fully support" Vrabel, allowing him to seek the counseling he desired despite four rounds of the draft still remaining.
